answer.rationale: Temporal coincidence (release 2h ago, latency climbing 90m) makes the new build the leading suspect, and rollback is the only candidate that can remove a causal agent rather than mask symptoms. memory_b2 explicitly forbids regional_failover while writes are hot — settlement peak with heavy writes is exactly that condition, and the stated objective bars losing customer writes, so failover is excluded regardless of how fast it recovered latency in March. add_capacity (memory_b3) worked for a *forecast* surge with lead time, not for an in-progress degradation, and would not help if the regression is code-path bound. route_read_replicas (memory_b5) relieved the primary of *read* load; here the pain is on the write path, so the mechanism does not transfer. enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) contained a *third-party* dependency failure; there is no partner outage signal here and failing fast would shed settlement writes at peak. I verify memory_b1 because it recorded a rollback that cleared an *error spike*, not a latency ramp — I need the original record to see whether the mechanism transfers to a gradual p99 climb and whether the 'no customer impact' claim held under write load. I verify memory_b6 to confirm staged release gating and canary cohorts still exist on this release path; if they do, I can roll back one cohort first and read the causal signal cheaply. If b6 shows no canary infrastructure, or b1 shows the prior rollback was done during a quiet window, I will reconsider before widening. Scale is a small guarded test rather than broad rollout: rolling the whole fleet back mid-settlement is itself a write-path event, and I do not yet have confirmation the release is causal — the latency ramp began 90 minutes ago against a 120-minute-old release, a 30-minute gap I cannot currently explain. Downstream risk: if the release carried a schema or data-format change, rolling back can strand or corrupt writes made under the new format; the guarded cohort must be checked for that before any expansion, and if such a change is present rollback becomes unsafe and I should hold for the next window instead.
